claims.text: Elevated-temperature stress–strain behavior of HfNbTaTiZr is influenced by its microstructure.
The distribution and interaction of dislocations influence the elevated-temperature response of HfNbTaTiZr.
In-situ neutron diffraction and transmission electron microscopy can elucidate the relevant dislocation-mediated response.
The initial HfNbTaTiZr material is polycrystalline and may have varying grain sizes and constituent-element distributions.
Elevated temperature and controlled mechanical loading drive dislocation dynamics and microstructural evolution.
Dislocation glide becomes thermally activated under the proposed elevated-temperature conditions.
Dislocation climb becomes thermally activated under the proposed elevated-temperature conditions.
The alloy composition and microstructure influence thermally activated dislocation glide and climb.
Relative to room temperature, elevated-temperature stress–strain behavior will be non-linear.
Relative to room temperature, thermal expansion will increase at elevated temperature.
Relative to room temperature, the elastic modulus will decrease at elevated temperature.
Elevated-temperature loading may produce strain hardening.
Elevated-temperature loading may produce texture evolution.
The proposed hypothesis is intended to apply from 500°C to 1000°C and from 0% to 10% strain.

contradictions.description: The temperature conversions are inconsistent: 500°C is approximately 773 K rather than 800 K, and 1000°C is approximately 1273 K rather than 1300 K. Thus the Celsius and kelvin limits do not denote exactly the same range.
